examples.en: Around then, I was getting ready to move.

examples.ko: 지난 가을이었으니까 그즈음 날씨가 꽤 쌀쌀했어요.
examples.en: It was last fall, so the weather was quite chilly around then.

examples.ko: 그즈음부터 친구가 연락을 잘 안 했어요.
examples.en: From around that time, my friend didn't contact me much.
The exam ended in March, so it must have been around then.

examples.ko: 그즈음 우리 동네에는 새 가게가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Around that time, a lot of new shops opened in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 작년 겨울 그즈음에는 뭐 하고 계셨어요?
examples.en: What were you doing around that time last winter?

explain: 정확한 날짜가 아니라 앞에서 말한 때의 앞뒤, 그러니까 대략 그 무렵을 가리켜요. 비슷한 말로 '그 무렵', '그맘때'가 있고, 말할 때는 '그때쯤'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It points to the rough time around a moment already mentioned, not an exact date. Similar expressions are '그 무렵' and '그맘때', and in speech people also say '그때쯤'.

examples.ko: 선생님 과목이 아니더라도 그쯤은 해 주실 수 있지 않을까요?
examples.en: Even if it isn't your subject, couldn't you do that much for us?

examples.ko: 오늘 회의는 그쯤으로 하고 점심 먹으러 가요.
examples.en: Let's leave today's meeting at that and go have lunch.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 여섯 시니까 그쯤 도착하면 돼요.
examples.en: The appointment is at six, so arriving around then is fine.
Enough of the fighting, let's make up now.
That much isn't hard, so I'll do it.
Just come expecting the cost to be about that much.

explain: '그 정도'를 줄인 느낌으로, 정도나 양, 때를 가볍게 가리켜요. '그쯤 하다'는 이제 그만하자는 뜻으로, '그쯤이야'는 별것 아니라는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels like a shortened '그 정도' and loosely points to a degree, amount or time. '그쯤 하다' means 'that's enough', and '그쯤이야' means 'that's nothing'.

examples.en: With the weekend here, the movie theaters are crowded.

examples.ko: 이번 여름 극장가는 한국 영화가 이끌고 있어요.
examples.en: This summer, Korean films are leading the movie theater scene.

examples.ko: 연말이 되면 극장가가 데이트하는 사람들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: At the end of the year, the theaters are packed with couples on dates.
Which movie is popular in theaters these days?
Movies aimed at the holiday theater season are being released.
For a while, the movie theater scene was very quiet too.

explain: 영화관이 모인 거리를 뜻하기도 하지만, 뉴스에서는 '지금 영화관 분위기나 흥행 상황' 전체를 말할 때 더 많이 나와요. '극장가에 ~ 바람이 불다'처럼 영화 개봉 소식에 자주 써요.
explain_en: It can mean a street full of cinemas, but in the news it often refers to the overall box-office mood of theaters. You will see it in phrases about movie releases and trends.

examples.en: Korea achieved modernization in a short time.

examples.ko: 산업 근대화는 사람들의 생활을 크게 바꿨어요.
examples.en: Industrial modernization greatly changed people's lives.

examples.ko: 근대화 과정에서 전통 문화가 많이 사라졌어요.
examples.en: A lot of traditional culture disappeared during modernization.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 일본의 근대화에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about Japan's modernization.
The rural modernization project began in the 1970s.

examples.ko: 근대화가 빨랐던 나라들은 도시화도 빨리 진행됐어요.
examples.en: Countries that modernized quickly also urbanized quickly.

explain: 주로 역사, 사회, 경제 수업이나 뉴스에서 나오는 말이에요. 건물이나 설비를 새로 고치는 일에는 '현대화'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in history, social studies, economics and the news. For upgrading buildings or equipment, people may use '현대화' instead.

examples.en: My new workplace is close to home, which is nice.
Please write your workplace address on the form.

examples.ko: 근무처가 바뀌면 회사에 바로 알려야 해요.
examples.en: If your workplace changes, you must tell the company right away.

examples.ko: 근무처에서 오는 전화는 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: I have to take calls that come from my workplace.

examples.ko: 지금 근무처까지 지하철로 사십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes forty minutes by subway to my current workplace.
Since I changed workplaces, I work fewer late nights.

explain: '직장'이 일하는 곳을 두루 말한다면 '근무처'는 서류의 칸 이름이나 연락처를 쓸 때 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '회사', '직장'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: '직장' is the general word for where you work, while '근무처' often appears as a field name on forms or contact details. In casual talk people usually say '회사' or '직장'.

examples.ko: 정확한 값은 몰라도 근사치는 말할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I don't know the exact value, but I can give an approximate one.

examples.ko: 계산기 없이 근사치부터 먼저 구해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's first work out an approximate value without a calculator.

examples.ko: 이건 근사치일 뿐이니까 정확한 숫자는 아니에요.
examples.en: This is only an approximation, so it isn't the exact number.

examples.ko: 제가 계산한 값은 실제 값에 가까운 근사치였어요.
examples.en: The value I calculated was a close approximation of the real value.
We usually write the approximate value of pi as 3.14.
Shall we compare the approximation with the actual value?

explain: 수학이나 통계에서 정확한 값 대신 가깝게 쓰는 수를 말해요. 일상에서는 '대략', '어림잡아'처럼 말하고, '근사치'는 숫자를 다루는 상황에서 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a number used instead of the exact value, mainly in math and statistics. In daily talk people say '대략' or '어림잡아', and '근사치' fits situations dealing with numbers.

examples.ko: 요즘 아이 성적이 가장 큰 근심거리예요.
examples.en: These days my child's grades are my biggest worry.

examples.ko: 근심거리가 없으면 잠이 잘 올 텐데요.
examples.en: If I had no worries, I could sleep well.
For my parents, worrying about me was always a concern.

examples.ko: 근심거리를 혼자 안고 있지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't carry your worries alone, tell someone.
Now that the exam is over, one worry is gone.

examples.ko: 건강 문제가 요즘 새 근심거리로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A health problem has become a new worry lately.

explain: '걱정거리'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '근심'은 조금 글이나 점잖은 말투에 어울리고, 일상 대화에서는 '걱정거리'를 더 자연스럽게 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '걱정거리'. '근심' sounds a bit more written or formal, and many people find '걱정거리' more natural in everyday talk.

examples.en: That actor is famous for his muscular build.

examples.ko: 운동을 오래 해서 팔이 근육질이 됐어요.
examples.en: After exercising for a long time, my arms became muscular.

examples.ko: 근육질인 사람이 꼭 힘이 센 건 아니에요.
examples.en: A muscular person is not always strong.
I'm more comfortable with a slim build than a muscular one.
A muscular model appears in the sportswear ad.

examples.ko: 근육질이 되고 싶으면 단백질을 잘 챙겨 먹어요.
examples.en: If you want to get muscular, make sure you eat enough protein.

explain: '근육'은 몸속 근육 자체이고, '근육질'은 근육이 발달한 몸이나 체형을 말해요. '근육질 몸', '근육질이다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '근육' means muscle itself, while '근육질' describes a body or build with well-developed muscles. You say '근육질 몸' or '근육질이다'.

examples.en: I got bitten by a mosquito and my arm is itchy.
My back is itchy, could you scratch it for me?
It itched so I kept scratching and it turned red.

examples.ko: 새 옷 때문에 목이 근질거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My neck itched because of the new clothes, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 상처가 아물 때는 근질거릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: A wound can feel itchy while it heals.

examples.ko: 몸이 근질거릴 땐 샤워하고 로션을 발라 보세요.
examples.en: When your body feels itchy, try showering and applying lotion.

explain: '가렵다'보다 살짝 간지럽고 자꾸 긁고 싶은 느낌이에요. '근질근질하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 병원에서 증상을 말할 때는 '가렵다'가 더 무난해요.

phrases.example: 비밀을 알고 나니 말하고 싶어서 입이 근질거려요.
phrases.en: Now that I know the secret, I'm itching to tell someone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하고 싶은 것을 참기 힘들 때 써요. 비밀이나 자랑거리처럼 꼭 말하고 싶은 얘기가 있을 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can hardly hold back something you want to say, such as a secret or something to brag about.

explain_en: Compared with '가렵다', it has a slightly tickly feeling that makes you want to scratch. It is almost interchangeable with '근질근질하다'. When describing symptoms at a clinic, '가렵다' is the safer choice.

examples.ko: 모기 물린 데가 근질근질해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The mosquito bite is itchy, so I can't sleep.
My scalp is itchy, should I change my shampoo?
My back is itchy, so my hand keeps going there.
I'm sweaty and my whole body feels itchy.

examples.ko: 근질근질한 곳을 긁지 말고 약을 발라요.
examples.en: Don't scratch the itchy spot, put medicine on it.
If your hands feel itchy, try washing them with cold water.

explain: '근질거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 상태를 말할 때는 '근질근질하다'를 많이 써요. 몸이 가려울 때뿐 아니라 뭔가 하고 싶어 가만히 있기 힘들 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 비가 그치니 밖에 나가고 싶어서 몸이 근질근질해요.
phrases.en: The rain stopped and I'm itching to go outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가만히 있기 힘들 만큼 움직이거나 뭔가를 하고 싶을 때 써요. 가려운 것과는 상관이 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so eager to move or do something that sitting still is hard. It has nothing to do with real itching.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '근질거리다', and '근질근질하다' is common for describing a state. Besides an itchy body, it is also used when you are restless to do something.

examples.en: This week's writing topic is 'travel'.

examples.ko: 일기를 쓰다 보면 글감이 저절로 생겨요.
examples.en: When you keep a diary, writing material comes naturally.

examples.ko: 좋은 글감을 찾으려고 산책을 자주 해요.
examples.en: I often take walks to find good material for writing.

examples.ko: 평범한 일상도 훌륭한 글감이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even ordinary daily life can become great writing material.
When an idea for writing comes to me, I note it down right away.

examples.ko: 오늘은 어떤 글감으로 글을 써 볼까요?
examples.en: What topic shall we write about today?

explain: 글을 쓸 때 소재로 삼을 이야기나 생각이에요. 글쓰기 수업이나 작가들이 '글감을 찾다', '글감이 떠오르다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means the story or idea you use as material for writing. Writing classes and authors often say '글감을 찾다' or '글감이 떠오르다'.

examples.en: The child looked at me with tears welling up in their eyes.
Tears welled up in my eyes while watching the movie.

examples.ko: 어머니는 눈물이 글썽여서 말을 잇지 못했어요.
examples.en: My mother's eyes filled with tears and she couldn't go on speaking.
When the presentation ended, the teacher's eyes filled with tears.

examples.ko: 그는 눈물을 글썽이는 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: He nodded with a tearful face.
My friend smiled and said they were fine even though their eyes were teary.

explain: 눈물이 눈에 고여 금방 떨어질 듯한 모습이에요. 완전히 우는 것보다 약해서, 흘러내리기 전의 모습에 써요. '눈물을 글썽이다'가 가장 흔한 짝이고 '그렁그렁하다'도 비슷해요.
explain_en: It describes tears pooling in the eyes as if about to fall. It is weaker than actually crying, and shows the moment before tears run down. '눈물을 글썽이다' is the most common pairing, and '그렁그렁하다' is similar.

examples.en: Well, I don't really know that either.
Hmm, I'll probably go on Friday.

examples.ko: 글쎄요, 제가 그걸 할 수 있을지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: Well, I'm not sure whether I can do that.

examples.ko: 글쎄요, 그 영화가 재미있을지는 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: Hmm, I'm not sure whether that movie will be fun.

examples.ko: 글쎄, 난 네 말이 무슨 얘긴지 하나도 모르겠어요.
examples.en: Well, I can't tell at all what you are talking about.
Hmm, it's a little hard to answer right now.

explain: 확신이 없거나 대답을 망설일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 '글쎄요', 친한 사이에는 '글쎄'라고 해요. '글쎄 ~라니까'처럼 상대가 못 믿을 때 강조하는 쓰임도 있어요.
explain_en: You use it when you are unsure or hesitate to answer. Say '글쎄요' to elders or strangers and '글쎄' with close friends. There is also an emphatic use, as in '글쎄 ~라니까', when the other person doesn't believe you.

examples.ko: 냄비 바닥에 눌은 밥을 숟가락으로 긁어내요.
examples.en: I scrape the scorched rice off the bottom of the pot with a spoon.
I scraped the sticker off the wall with a knife.
I scooped out the watermelon flesh to make fruit punch.

examples.ko: 유리창에 낀 얼음을 긁어내느라 손이 시렸어요.
examples.en: My hands were cold from scraping the ice off the window.

examples.ko: 병 안쪽에 남은 잼까지 싹 긁어내요.
examples.en: I scrape out even the jam left inside the jar.

examples.ko: 오래된 페인트를 긁어내고 새로 칠해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to scrape off the old paint and repaint.

explain: 붙어 있거나 속에 남은 것을 도구로 긁어서 떼어 내거나 파내는 거예요. 반대로 흩어진 것을 한곳으로 모을 때는 '긁어모으다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means using a tool to scrape off something stuck on, or to scoop out what remains inside. For gathering scattered things into one place, use '긁어모으다' instead.

examples.en: I raked the fallen leaves together and piled them in one place.
I scraped together my allowance and bought a gift for my friend.
Even if I scrape together all my money, it's not enough.

examples.ko: 흩어진 쌀알을 손으로 긁어모아 봉지에 담았어요.
examples.en: I gathered the scattered grains of rice by hand and put them in a bag.
My friends held a flea market to scrape some money together.

examples.ko: 동전을 긁어모으면 커피 한 잔은 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If I gather all my coins, I can buy one cup of coffee.

explain: 흩어져 있는 것을 한곳으로 끌어모으는 거예요. 돈을 여기저기서 힘들게 겨우 모았다는 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 정리해서 차곡차곡 모을 때는 '모으다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means pulling scattered things together in one spot. It is also often used for money, with the feeling of barely scraping it together from here and there. For neatly saving up, plain '모으다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: He scratched his head as if embarrassed.
When asked a question, he laughed while scratching the back of his head.

examples.ko: 아이가 코를 긁적이면서 대답을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The child scratched their nose and couldn't answer.

examples.ko: 어색할 때 저도 모르게 뺨을 긁적여요.
examples.en: When I feel awkward, I scratch my cheek without realizing it.

examples.ko: 동생이 머리를 긁적이는 걸 보니 뭔가 잘못했나 봐요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is scratching their head, so they must have done something wrong.
My friend was scratching the back of their neck out of embarrassment.

explain: 가려워서보다는 쑥스럽거나 난처할 때 손으로 슬쩍 긁는 동작에 자주 써요. 그냥 몸을 긁는 것은 '긁다'라고 해요. '머리를 긁적이다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is often used for lightly scratching with a hand when you feel shy or awkward, not because of real itching. Ordinary scratching is just '긁다'. '머리를 긁적이다' is the most common pairing.

examples.en: In the movie, thieves stole gold bars.
Gold bars are stored in the bank vault.

examples.ko: 금괴 한 개가 얼마나 무거운지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you know how heavy a single gold bar is?
I saw news that gold bars were found under the sea.

examples.ko: 금괴는 값이 비싸서 아무나 살 수 없어요.
examples.en: Gold bars are expensive, so not just anyone can buy them.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에는 금괴를 숨긴 보물섬이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Old stories often feature treasure islands where gold bars are hidden.

explain: 금을 막대 모양으로 만든 덩어리예요. 이야기나 영화에서 보물로 자주 나오고, 투자 이야기에서는 '금'이나 '골드바'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is gold cast into a bar shape. It often appears as treasure in stories and movies, and in investment talk people also say '금' or '골드바'.

examples.en: This year's budget hasn't been decided yet.

examples.ko: 금년도 신입 사원 모집이 곧 시작돼요.
examples.en: Recruitment of this year's new employees will start soon.
There are two hundred graduates this year in total.

examples.ko: 이 장학금은 금년도에 입학한 학생에게만 줘요.
examples.en: This scholarship is given only to students who entered this year.

examples.ko: 금년도 목표를 달성하려면 더 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: To reach this year's goal, we have to try harder.

examples.ko: 금년도 세금 신고를 아직 못 했어요.
examples.en: I haven't filed my taxes for this year yet.

explain: '올해'와 같은 뜻이지만 공지, 공문서, 뉴스처럼 딱딱한 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '올해'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means the same as '올해', but it appears in notices, official documents and news, which sound stiff. In everyday talk, '올해' is more natural.

examples.en: When my grandfather smiles, you can see his gold tooth.

examples.ko: 치과에서 금니로 씌우는 데 돈이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: Getting a gold crown at the dentist cost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할머니의 금니가 신기해 보였어요.
examples.en: As a child, my grandmother's gold tooth looked fascinating to me.

examples.ko: 요즘은 금니보다 도자기 치아를 많이 해요.
examples.en: These days many people get ceramic teeth rather than gold ones.
A gold tooth glittered inside his smiling mouth.

examples.ko: 충치 치료 후에 어금니를 금니로 씌웠어요.
examples.en: After treating the cavity, I had my molar capped with gold.

explain: 금으로 씌우거나 때운 이를 말해요. 같은 방식으로 '은니'라는 말도 있어요. 요즘은 다른 재료를 쓰는 경우가 많아서 옛날 어른들 이야기에 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a tooth capped or filled with gold. By the same pattern there is also '은니' for silver. Other materials are common now, so it comes up more often in stories about older people.

examples.en: Yeouido is Korea's representative financial district.

examples.ko: 점심시간이 되면 금융가 식당이 직장인들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: At lunchtime, restaurants in the financial district are packed with office workers.
Wall Street in New York is famous as a global financial district.
There are many banks and securities firms near the financial district.

examples.ko: 저는 금융가 쪽에 있는 회사로 출근해요.
examples.en: I commute to a company in the financial district area.
On weekends the financial district is very quiet.

explain: 은행과 증권사가 모여 있는 거리나 지역, 즉 장소를 가리켜요. 사람들이나 업계 전체를 말할 때는 '금융계'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a place, the streets or area where banks and securities firms cluster. For the people or industry as a whole, use '금융계'.

examples.ko: 그 소식은 금융계에 큰 충격을 줬어요.
examples.en: The news was a big shock to the financial world.
My uncle worked in the financial industry for a long time.
People in the financial world are sensitive to interest rate changes.

examples.ko: 금융계 인사가 새 정부에 합류한다는 기사가 났어요.
examples.en: An article said a figure from the financial world will join the new government.

examples.ko: 요즘 금융계에서는 인공지능 기술을 많이 써요.
examples.en: These days the financial industry uses a lot of AI technology.

examples.ko: 금융계로 취직하고 싶어서 경제 공부를 해요.
examples.en: I want to get a job in finance, so I study economics.

explain: '-계'는 어떤 분야의 사람들과 사회를 뜻해서, 금융계는 금융 분야 전체를 말해요. '연예계', '의료계'처럼 쓰는 말이고, 거리나 지역은 '금융가'예요.
explain_en: '-계' means the people and society of a field, so '금융계' means the finance field as a whole. It works like '연예계' or '의료계', while a district is '금융가'.

examples.en: I went to the jewelry shop to buy wedding rings.
I got my watch strap fixed at the neighborhood jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 금은방 사장님이 반지 크기를 재 주셨어요.
examples.en: The jewelry shop owner measured my ring size.

examples.ko: 할머니가 금은방에서 돌 반지를 맞춰 오셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother had a first-birthday ring made at the jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 금은방 앞을 지나다가 예쁜 목걸이를 봤어요.
examples.en: Passing in front of a jewelry shop, I saw a pretty necklace.

examples.ko: 요즘은 금은방보다 온라인에서 액세서리를 사는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days more people buy accessories online than at jewelry shops.

explain: 금과 은으로 만든 장신구를 파는 동네 가게예요. 반지, 목걸이를 사거나 금을 팔 때 가는 곳이고, 백화점 매장은 보통 '귀금속 매장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a small neighborhood shop selling gold and silver jewelry. People go there to buy rings and necklaces or to sell gold, while a department store counter is usually called '귀금속 매장'.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 정부가 금지곡을 정해서 방송하지 못하게 했어요.
examples.en: In the past, the government designated banned songs and kept them off the air.
That song was once banned.
I'm curious why it became a banned song.

examples.ko: 금지곡이었던 노래들이 요즘 다시 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: Songs that were once banned are becoming popular again.
I looked up this singer's list of banned songs.
The lyrics became a problem and it was designated a banned song.

explain: 방송이나 공연에서 부르거나 틀지 못하게 막은 노래예요. 한국 대중음악의 역사 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 가사나 사회 분위기 때문에 한동안 방송이 막혔던 노래를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is a song that was prohibited from being sung or played in broadcasts and performances. It often appears in stories about Korean pop music history, for songs kept off the air for a time because of their lyrics or the social climate.

examples.en: My grandfather wears gold-rimmed glasses.
A gold rim runs around the edge of the plate.

examples.ko: 금테 두른 거울이 거실에 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A mirror with a gold frame hangs in the living room.
Gold-rimmed glasses suit your face well.
The gold coating peeled off, so I bought new glasses.

examples.ko: 컵에 금테가 있어서 전자레인지에 넣으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: The cup has a gold rim, so you shouldn't put it in the microwave.

explain: 안경이나 그릇, 액자의 가장자리를 금빛으로 두른 테를 말해요. '금테 안경'처럼 쓰는 경우가 가장 많아요.
explain_en: It is a gold-colored rim around the edge of glasses, dishes or frames. The most common use is '금테 안경'.

examples.ko: 놀이기구가 급강하하자 탑승객들이 일제히 비명을 질렀어요.
examples.en: When the ride dropped suddenly, the riders all screamed at once.
They say the temperature will plunge from the afternoon.
The plane dropped suddenly for a moment because of turbulence.

examples.ko: 밤사이 기온이 급강하해서 두꺼운 옷을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: The temperature plunged overnight, so I took out thick clothes.
The bird spotted its food, swooped down and snatched it.
I felt a sudden dropping sensation and I was scared.

explain: 높이나 온도가 갑자기 뚝 내려갈 때 써요. 날씨 뉴스와 비행기, 놀이기구 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 값이나 주가가 갑자기 떨어질 때는 '급락하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when height or temperature falls abruptly, and appears often in weather reports and talk of planes and rides. For prices or stocks suddenly falling, '급락하다' is used more.

examples.en: This road is steep, so it's dangerous in winter.
Go down slowly on steep sections.

examples.ko: 집으로 가는 길이 급경사여서 자전거를 끌고 가요.
examples.en: The road home is steep, so I push my bike.
I was out of breath from climbing the steep slope.
Near the mountaintop the steep slope continues.

examples.ko: 급경사 도로에는 미끄럼 방지 시설이 있어요.
examples.en: Steep roads have anti-slip facilities.

explain: 비탈이 매우 가파른 곳이에요. 반대말은 '완경사'이고, 형용사로는 '가파르다'를 써서 '길이 가파르다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a very steep incline. The opposite is '완경사', and with an adjective you can say '길이 가파르다' for the same idea.

examples.en: Because of moving, I put my house up for a quick sale.
Urgent-sale items come out cheaper than the market price.
I went to see a car that was listed for a quick sale.
I asked the real estate agent if there were any urgent sales.

examples.ko: 급매 물건이라도 꼼꼼히 확인하고 사야 해요.
examples.en: Even for an urgent-sale item, you should check carefully before buying.

examples.ko: 빨리 팔려고 가격을 내려서 급매로 올렸어요.
examples.en: To sell quickly, I lowered the price and listed it as an urgent sale.

explain: 집이나 차를 급하게 팔아야 해서 값을 낮추어 내놓는 거래예요. 부동산 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 그런 물건은 '급매물'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a sale where the seller needs to sell fast and lowers the price. It appears often in real estate talk, and such items are also called '급매물'.

examples.en: The car ahead stopped, so I slammed on the brakes.

examples.ko: 급브레이크를 밟으면 뒤차가 놀랄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you brake suddenly, the car behind may be startled.
I was startled by the sound of screeching brakes.
Hard braking is very dangerous on snowy roads.
A child ran out, so I braked hard.
The coffee all spilled because of the sudden braking.

explain: '급브레이크를 밟다'처럼 쓰는 짝말이 가장 흔해요. 차가 갑자기 서는 상황 자체는 '급정거'라고 해요.
explain_en: The most common pairing is '급브레이크를 밟다'. The situation of a vehicle stopping suddenly is called '급정거'.

examples.ko: 공에 급소를 맞은 선수가 한참 일어나지 못했어요.
examples.en: The player hit by the ball in a vulnerable spot couldn't get up for a while.

examples.ko: 몸에는 세게 치면 위험한 급소가 있어요.
examples.en: The body has vital spots that are dangerous if hit hard.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 목은 다치면 위험한 급소라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said the neck is a vital spot that is dangerous to injure.

examples.ko: 발표 끝에 나온 질문이 우리 계획의 급소를 건드렸어요.
examples.en: A question at the end of the presentation touched the weak point of our plan.

examples.ko: 그 문제는 회사의 급소라서 말하기 조심스러워요.
examples.en: That issue is the company's sore spot, so I'm careful about mentioning it.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 급소만 콕 짚어서 말해요.
examples.en: That friend speaks by pinpointing only the crucial weak spots.

explain: 몸에서 다치면 크게 위험하거나 아픈 곳이에요. 비유로 일이나 사람의 가장 약한 부분, 핵심 약점을 가리킬 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그의 한마디가 정확히 내 급소를 찔렀어요.
phrases.en: His one remark hit my weak spot exactly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 가장 아파하거나 감추고 싶은 약점을 정확히 건드릴 때 써요. 말이나 질문이 날카로울 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a remark or question touches exactly the point someone is most sensitive about or wants to hide.

explain_en: It is a spot on the body where an injury is especially dangerous or painful. Figuratively it also means the weakest, most crucial point of a matter or person.

examples.ko: 학교는 형편이 어려운 학생에게 급식비를 보조해요.
examples.en: The school helps students in difficult circumstances with their meal fees.
The school meal fee must be paid by the end of each month.

examples.ko: 이번 달 급식비가 얼마인지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how much the school meal fee is this month.

examples.ko: 급식비를 못 낸 학생은 선생님께 말씀드리세요.
examples.en: Students who couldn't pay the meal fee should tell the teacher.

examples.ko: 형제가 둘이면 급식비가 두 배로 들어요.
examples.en: With two siblings, the meal fees cost double.
I signed up for automatic payment of my sibling's school meal fee.

explain: 학교에서 먹는 점심 같은 단체 급식에 내는 돈이에요. 학교 공지문이나 가정통신문에 자주 나오고, 집에서 쓰는 식비와는 구분해요.
explain_en: It is the money paid for group meals such as school lunch. It often appears in school notices and letters to parents, and is separate from household food expenses.

examples.en: I get along well with my classmates.
I finished my homework with a classmate's help.

examples.ko: 급우 중에 노래를 잘하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: Among my classmates, there is a friend who sings well.
I quickly became close with my new classmate.

examples.ko: 급우 한 명이 전학을 가서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: One classmate transferred to another school, which is a pity.
The teacher told us to help our classmates.

explain: 같은 반 친구를 뜻하지만 글이나 공식적인 말에서 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '반 친구'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means a classmate but is mostly used in writing or formal speech. In everyday conversation, '반 친구' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 급정거 때문에 뒷좌석에 둔 짐이 앞으로 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the sudden stop, the bags on the back seat spilled forward.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 뛰어나온 탓에 급정거가 불가피했어요.
examples.en: A child suddenly ran out, so a sudden stop was unavoidable.
The bus stopped suddenly and the passengers staggered.

examples.ko: 택시가 갑자기 급정거하는 바람에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The taxi suddenly braked hard and I was startled.

examples.ko: 앞차가 급정거할 때를 대비해서 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: Keep your distance in case the car ahead stops suddenly.

examples.ko: 그 차가 급정거했지만 늦어서 가볍게 부딪혔어요.
examples.en: That car braked hard but too late, and they bumped lightly.

explain: 자동차나 버스가 갑자기 서는 상황에 써요. '급정차'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 급브레이크를 밟아 확 서는 장면에 잘 어울려요. 사람이 갑자기 멈출 때는 '갑자기 멈춰 서다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a car or bus stops suddenly. It is almost the same as '급정차' and fits scenes of slamming the brakes. When a person stops abruptly, say '갑자기 멈춰 서다'.

examples.ko: 급정차 때문에 승객 몇 명이 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: A few passengers fell because of the sudden stop.

examples.ko: 버스 안에서는 급정차에 대비해 손잡이를 잡으세요.
examples.en: On the bus, hold the handle in case of a sudden stop.
Service was briefly delayed by a sudden subway stop.
I screamed, startled by the abrupt stop.
A bus that stops suddenly often is uncomfortable to ride.
After the sudden stop, the driver asked if everyone was okay.

explain: 버스, 지하철, 기차가 갑자기 서는 일이에요. '급정거'와 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 써도 되고, 안내 방송이나 뉴스에서는 '급정차'가 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a bus, subway or train stopping suddenly. It is nearly the same as '급정거' and can be swapped, and '급정차' often appears in announcements and news.

examples.en: The car ahead stopped suddenly, so I stopped in a hurry too.
The bus stopped abruptly and I spilled my milk.
The train made a sudden stop because of a signal problem.
The taxi driver stopped suddenly and looked back.

examples.ko: 급정차하면 뒤따르는 차와 부딪힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you stop suddenly, you may be hit by the car behind.
A stray cat darted in and the car stopped suddenly.

explain: '급정거하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 차나 열차가 갑자기 설 때 써요. '급정차'가 뉴스와 안내문에 자주 나오고, 말할 때는 '급브레이크를 밟다'도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '급정거하다' and is used when a vehicle or train stops abruptly. '급정차' appears often in news and notices, and in speech people also say '급브레이크를 밟다'.

examples.en: I ate too quickly and got sudden indigestion.
I got sudden indigestion last evening and was in pain all night.
I once went to the emergency room because of sudden indigestion.

examples.ko: 너무 빨리 먹으면 급체할 수 있으니 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: You can get sudden indigestion if you eat too fast, so eat slowly.

examples.ko: 급체한 것 같아서 오늘은 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: I think I have indigestion, so I only ate porridge today.
My sibling's face turned pale, probably from sudden indigestion.

explain: '체하다'보다 갑자기 심하게 얹혔을 때 써요. 일상에서는 보통 '체했어요'라고 말하고, '급체'는 증상이 갑작스럽고 힘들다는 걸 강조할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when indigestion hits suddenly and severely, more than '체하다'. In daily talk people usually say '체했어요', and '급체' stresses that the symptoms are sudden and hard.

examples.en: You have to slow down in sharp-turn sections.
My body leaned to one side because of the sharp turn.

examples.ko: 이 도로에는 급회전이 많아서 운전이 어려워요.
examples.en: This road has many sharp turns, so it's hard to drive.
I screamed when the ride made a sharp turn.
The luggage fell over when we made a sharp turn.

examples.ko: 앞에 급회전 표지판이 보이면 천천히 가세요.
examples.en: If you see a sharp-turn sign ahead, go slowly.

explain: 갑자기 크게 방향을 바꾸는 일이에요. 도로의 심하게 굽은 길은 '급커브'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is suddenly and sharply changing direction. A sharply bent road is also commonly called '급커브'.

examples.en: Our class motto is 'Let's smile today too'.

examples.ko: 급훈이 칠판 위에 크게 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The class motto is posted big above the blackboard.
We voted to decide this year's class motto.
The teacher came with a class motto they made up themselves.
Class mottos in the past often had words like 'diligence' or 'effort'.

examples.ko: 급훈 덕분인지 우리 반은 분위기가 밝아요.
examples.en: Maybe thanks to the motto, our class has a bright atmosphere.

explain: 한 학급이 지키려고 정한 목표나 가르침이에요. 한국 학교에서는 교실 앞에 걸어 두는 경우가 많고, 학교 전체의 가르침은 '교훈'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the goal or lesson a class chooses to live by. In Korean schools it is often displayed at the front of the room, while the motto of the whole school is '교훈'.

examples.en: Agricultural mechanization greatly reduced the need for labor.
The factory's mechanization is almost complete.
As mechanization advanced, jobs changed.
Some people are worried because of mechanization.
The mechanization of rice planting happened long ago.
Thanks to mechanization, production speed increased.

explain: 사람이 하던 일을 기계가 대신하게 되는 변화예요. 농업, 공장, 산업 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '자동화'는 사람 손 없이 저절로 돌아가는 데 더 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is the change of machines taking over work people used to do. It appears often in talk of farming, factories and industry, while '자동화' focuses more on things running by themselves without human hands.

examples.en: The company decided to mechanize the packaging work.

examples.ko: 농장은 수확 과정을 기계화해서 인력이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The farm mechanized its harvesting process, so the workforce shrank.
If we mechanize all the work, will costs go down?
Since the factory was mechanized, defective products have decreased.

examples.ko: 사람 손이 필요한 부분은 기계화하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Parts that need a human hand are hard to mechanize.

examples.ko: 이 작업을 기계화하려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Mechanizing this task costs a lot of money.

explain: 사람이 하던 일을 기계로 하도록 바꾼다는 뜻이라 주어는 보통 회사나 사람이에요. '포장을 기계화하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 명사 '기계화'와 달리 동작을 나타내요.
explain_en: The subject is usually a company or person who switches work over to machines, and it takes an object, as in '포장을 기계화하다'. Unlike the noun '기계화', it expresses the action.

examples.en: The cold developed into bronchitis.

examples.ko: 기침이 오래가서 병원에서 기관지염 진단을 받았어요.
examples.en: My cough lasted long, so I was diagnosed with bronchitis at the hospital.

examples.ko: 기관지염에 걸리면 목이 아프고 기침이 나요.
examples.en: When you have bronchitis, your throat hurts and you cough.

examples.ko: 기관지염 때문에 일주일 동안 약을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I took medicine for a week because of bronchitis.
Many of my friends suffer from bronchitis in winter.

examples.ko: 기관지염이 낫도록 따뜻한 물을 자주 마셨어요.
examples.en: I drank warm water often so the bronchitis would heal.

explain: 숨 쉬는 길인 기관지에 염증이 생긴 병이에요. 병원에서는 '급성 기관지염', '만성 기관지염'처럼 나누어 말해요.
explain_en: It is an illness where the bronchi, the airways, become inflamed. Doctors speak of '급성 기관지염' (acute) and '만성 기관지염' (chronic).

examples.ko: 기능성 화장품은 피부 고민에 맞춰 나와요.
examples.en: Functional cosmetics are made for specific skin concerns.

examples.ko: 이 운동복은 땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재예요.
examples.en: This sportswear is a functional fabric that dries sweat quickly.

examples.ko: 기능성 식품을 먹기 전에 성분을 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check the ingredients before eating functional foods.

examples.ko: 디자인보다 기능성을 먼저 보고 신발을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose shoes by looking at functionality before design.

examples.ko: 기능성 양말이라 오래 걸어도 발이 편해요.
examples.en: These are functional socks, so my feet are comfortable even after long walks.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 기능성이 뛰어나서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This bag is popular because its functionality is outstanding.

explain: '땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재'처럼 보통 다른 명사 앞에 붙어 특별한 기능을 넣은 물건을 말해요. 혼자 '기능성이 좋다'고 하면 겉모양보다 쓰임이 좋다는 쪽이에요. '실용성'은 쓸모가 있는 정도이고, '기능성'은 특정 기능을 넣었다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It usually attaches to another noun, as in '땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재', for items with a built-in special function. On its own, '기능성이 좋다' means it works well rather than just looks good. '실용성' is how useful something is, while '기능성' stresses a specific built-in function.

examples.ko: 천막을 칠 자리가 정해지면 먼저 기다랗게 골을 파요.
examples.en: Once the spot for the tent is decided, first dig a long trench.
I picked the persimmon with a long stick.
The puppy ran over, flapping its long ears.
After passing through the long tunnel, the sea appeared.
The road is so long that I can't see the end.
They are a pianist with long, slender fingers.

explain: '길다'보다 폭이 좁고 길쭉하게 늘어진 모양이 눈에 보일 때 써요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 '기다래요', '기다란'처럼 바뀌어요.
explain_en: Compared with '길다', it is used when you can picture a narrow, stretched-out shape. It is an ㅎ irregular, so it becomes '기다래요' and '기다란'.

examples.en: He stood leaning against the wall, waiting for his friend.
Don't just stand leaning on the door frame, come in.
People leaning on the railing watched the fireworks.
If you lean against the tree, you can feel the cool breeze.
I leaned against the wall and got paint on my clothes.
My grandfather walks slowly, leaning on his cane.

explain: '기대다'와 '서다'가 합쳐진 말로, 어딘가에 몸을 기댄 채 서 있는 모습이에요. 앉아서 기댈 때는 '기대앉다'를 써요.
explain_en: It combines '기대다' and '서다' and describes standing while leaning against something. When you lean while sitting, use '기대앉다'.
